units.title: Still wines · session 1: structure and origin

evidencePrompts.prompt: Describe the appearance, aromas, flavours and structure you observed in this still wine. Keep sensory evidence separate from a possible origin.
Explain your quality judgement using observed balance, intensity, complexity and finish.
Explain whether this wine could benefit from bottle ageing, and identify the sensory evidence and limits behind your view.
Which observations might support a grape, climate or regional hypothesis? Give at least one plausible alternative.
Which inference about this wine is least secure, and what further observation would test it?

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all six still wines through their observed acidity, body, tannin where relevant, flavour development, quality and ageing potential. Explain which contrasts might support different growing environments without treating them as proof of origin.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Review all six assessments. Which conclusions are supported by the strongest sensory evidence, and which need another explanation or a further tasting?

units.title: Still wines · session 2: style and production

evidencePrompts.prompt: Record the appearance, aromas, flavours and structure of this still wine as you observed them in the glass.
Justify the quality level from the wine's balance, concentration, complexity and finish rather than a guessed label or price.
State a drinking-window judgement and the evidence for development or decline in this particular wine.
What sensory clues might reflect grape growing or winemaking choices? Separate the observation from each possible production explanation.
Identify a competing style or production explanation and say what evidence would distinguish it.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all six still wines for fruit character, structural balance, possible production effects, quality and ageing potential. Explain similarities and differences with evidence from each glass.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Revisit the six wine notes after comparison. Which production or style inferences became stronger, which remain tentative, and why?

units.title: Sparkling wines

evidencePrompts.prompt: Describe what you actually saw, smelled and tasted. Include the mousse or bubbles and the wine's structure.
Justify your quality judgement with specific balance, intensity, complexity and finish evidence.
Explain your drinking-window and ageing judgement from the wine in the glass. What might develop, and what might limit it?
Which observed clues may support a sparkling style or production method? Separate what you sensed from any production inference.
Which conclusion is least secure? Name an observation or alternative explanation that could change it.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all three sparkling wines using observed mousse, aromas, structure, quality and ageing potential. Explain the evidence behind the differences.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Review your three conclusions: which observations support them, and which observations or alternative explanations weaken them?

units.title: Fortified wines

evidencePrompts.prompt: Describe what you actually saw, smelled and tasted, including sweetness, alcohol, structure and flavour development.
Justify your quality judgement with specific balance, intensity, complexity and finish evidence.
Explain your drinking-window and ageing judgement from the wine in the glass. What might develop, and what might limit it?
Which observed clues may support a fortification or maturation style? Separate sensory evidence from a production inference.
Which conclusion is least secure? Name an observation or alternative explanation that could change it.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all three fortified wines using observed sweetness, alcohol, maturation clues, structure, quality and ageing potential. Explain the evidence behind the differences.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Review your three conclusions: which observations support them, and which observations or alternative explanations weaken them?
